title: All Home rows set isFocusableInTouchMode=true on phone — opposite of VOD/Series touch-passthrough pattern; grid becomes a focus candidate on empty-area taps
symptom: On a phone, a finger-down on a Home row's EMPTY area (the inter-card gutters / leading padding / area past the last card) lets the Leanback grid itself grab focus, and a horizontal drag begun there can hitch as the grid claims focus on ACTION_DOWN. Taps that land squarely ON a poster card still reach the card (its own focusableInTouchMode=true wins under descendantFocusability=afterDescendants), so the auditor's 'first taps land on the empty row / need a second press' is overstated for on-card taps. The defect is real but narrower: it is friction on empty-area / drag-start touches, plus a needless focus contender during scroll.
rootCause: HomeFragment.bindViews() (~line 503-509) loops all 8 static HorizontalGridViews on phone and sets grid.isFocusableInTouchMode = true; the dynamic genre/BYW rows do the same (~line 1291: isFocusableInTouchMode = !DeviceUtils.isTV(...)). This is the exact inverse of VodFragment (lines 85-86: posterGrid.descendantFocusability = FOCUS_AFTER_DESCENDANTS + isFocusableInTouchMode = false) and SeriesFragment (lines 83-84, identical). All static rows already declare descendantFocusability='afterDescendants' in fragment_home.xml (e.g. lines 301, 338), and the poster card root (item_poster_card.xml line 12) is itself focusableInTouchMode=true — so on-card taps go to the card. The grid being focusableInTouchMode only changes behavior when the touch is NOT on a focusable child (empty grid space), where the grid now self-focuses instead of doing nothing. The comment at line 502 ('let touch events pass directly to grid children') states the goal; setting the grid focusable-in-touch achieves the opposite intent and contradicts the codebase's own proven touch-passthrough idiom.
fix: Change both sites to match VOD/Series: at HomeFragment.kt:507 set grid.isFocusableInTouchMode = false (and optionally grid.descendantFocusability = FOCUS_AFTER_DESCENDANTS, though the XML already sets it), and at HomeFragment.kt:1291 set isFocusableInTouchMode = false (or drop the line so the default false applies on phone — the dynamic grids already set descendantFocusability = FOCUS_AFTER_DESCENDANTS at line 1292). Cards keep focusable=true + foreground=selectableItemBackground, so taps and horizontal drags reach them cleanly and the grid stops competing for the down event.
correction: Symptom overstated. With descendantFocusability=afterDescendants on the grids (XML lines 301/338) AND focusableInTouchMode=true on the poster card root (item_poster_card.xml:12), taps that land ON a card DO reach the card — the child wins focus over the parent. The grid's isFocusableInTouchMode=true only bites for taps on EMPTY grid area (gutters, padding, beyond last card) and as an extra focus contender during a drag-start. So 'first taps land on the empty row and need a second press' is not how it generally behaves on-card. The fix is still correct and worth doing (it matches the proven VOD/Series pattern and removes a needless touch focus candidate), but the user-facing impact is narrower than described. Severity P1 is defensible given it contradicts the working pattern and plausibly contributes to the 'menus not scrolling properly' complaint on drag-start, but it is borderline P2.

title: Home is a 10-foot TV layout with no portrait path; tall TV-sized rows + 24dp gaps bury content below the fold on a phone
symptom: In portrait on a phone the hero (runtime-scaled to 45% of screen height) plus the first 185dp poster row (170dp on small phones) plus 24dp section gaps fill most of the viewport, so a user sees the hero and at most one partial row and must scroll through tall TV-sized rails to reach content. It reads as a shrunken TV home, not a phone home. This is real but usability-degrading, not broken — everything still scrolls.
rootCause: There is only one layout/fragment_home.xml (shared by phone) plus a layout-television variant; no layout-port or phone-specific arrangement exists. Row heights are fixed at 185dp (values/dimens.xml:46-53; 170dp in values-sw320dp/dimens.xml) with layout_marginTop=24dp on every section label (fragment_home.xml e.g. lines 320, 348). The hero is NOT a fixed 200dp at runtime as the auditor stated: fragment_home.xml:37 sets layout_height=@dimen/hero_height, but HomeFragment.kt:203-207 OVERRIDES it to screenHeight * hero_height_percent/100, and on phones hero_height_percent=45 (values/integers.xml:3) — so the effective hero is ~45% of the actual screen, not 200dp/170dp. Still ~45% viewport + 185dp rows + 24dp gaps pushes rails below the fold.
fix: Add phone-tuned dimens in the values/ bucket (it is the phone default): shrink row_*_height to ~130-150dp and reduce label topMargin from 24dp to ~12dp, while keeping TV sizes in values-television/dimens.xml. Optionally lower hero_height_percent for phones (currently 45) so more rails show above the fold. Pure dimension/integer overrides — no code change. Note 24dp margins are hardcoded in XML so they would need extraction to a @dimen to override per bucket.
correction: Two corrections. (1) The hero is NOT a fixed 200dp/170dp at runtime — HomeFragment.kt:205-207 overrides the XML @dimen/hero_height to 45% of screen height on phone (hero_height_percent=45 in values/integers.xml). The auditor cited the dimens as the live value; they are only the pre-runtime placeholder. (2) Severity lowered P1 -> P2: the screen is fully usable and scrolls correctly; it is density/below-the-fold friction (polish-to-moderate), not a 'badly degraded but usable' P1. The 24dp label margins are hardcoded in XML (e.g. line 320), so the proposed 'pure dimens override' fix needs those values extracted to a @dimen first; the row-height override works as described.

title: Hero swipe GestureDetector returns true from onDown, contending with vertical page scroll when a drag starts on the hero
symptom: When a vertical scroll is begun with the finger on the hero banner (top of page), the hero touch listener consumes the down event, so the first vertical drag from the hero can feel sticky / not scroll the page until the finger leaves the hero region. Only fires on phone (setupHeroSwipeGesture is gated to non-TV at line 227).
rootCause: setupHeroSwipeGesture() (~line 1748-1777) installs heroContainer.setOnTouchListener { _, event -> gestureDetector.onTouchEvent(event) } and the SimpleOnGestureListener overrides onDown to return true (line 1774). Returning the gesture-detector result claims the down on the hero. The NestedScrollView can still steal the gesture once it crosses its vertical touch slop (NestedScrollView.onInterceptTouchEvent), so this is mitigated, not catastrophic — hence P2. onFling already gates on horizontal dominance (abs(deltaX) < 80 returns false, line 1759) so a vertical drag won't trigger a hero change; the residual issue is purely the consumed down event causing initial stickiness.
fix: Have the touch listener return false (or call gestureDetector.onTouchEvent(event) and then return false) so the NestedScrollView reliably receives the motion, OR change onDown to return false. The fling is already horizontal-gated (abs(deltaX) < 80 guard at line 1759), so returning false from the listener does not break the swipe-to-change-hero feature.
correction: Confirmed onDown returns true (line 1774) and the listener returns the gesture result (line 1776). One clarification to the auditor's root cause: onFling ALREADY guards horizontal dominance (abs(deltaX) < 80 at line 1759), so vertical drags do not accidentally rotate the hero — the only live problem is the consumed ACTION_DOWN causing initial stickiness, which NestedScrollView's own slop-based interception largely recovers from. P2 is correct.

title: Hero pagination dots are tappable on phone but only ~8dp tall — far below the 48dp Material touch-target minimum
symptom: On a phone the hero page-indicator dots are made clickable (jump to that featured item) but each dot is 8dp tall and 8dp wide (24dp wide when active), with only a 6dp end margin, so they are hard to hit accurately and mis-taps are likely.
rootCause: updateHeroIndicators() (~line 641-671) builds each dot with dotHeight = 8.dp and dotWidth = 8.dp (24.dp active), sets isClickable = true and a setOnClickListener for phone (lines 657-667). The clickable bounds equal the visual 8dp dot — no TouchDelegate, no expanded hit rect.
fix: Keep the 8dp visual dot but expand the touchable region to >=48dp: wrap each dot in a 48dp-min container, or attach an android.view.TouchDelegate on hero_indicators that grows each dot's hit rect to 48dp, or give the dot View a 48dp layout height/width with the visible drawable centered/inset.
correction: Confirmed exactly as described — dotHeight=8.dp, dotWidth 8.dp/24.dp, isClickable=true on phone, no expanded hit area. P3 is correct (polish; dots are a convenience, hero also rotates automatically and is swipeable).

title: BrowseCardFocusHelper neighbor-dimming is keyed on D-pad focus; on touch it can leave cards stuck at 0.50/0.65 alpha
symptom: On a phone, if a card gains focus (e.g. a tap the grid converts to focus), the helper dims neighbouring cards to 65%/50% alpha. Because touch focus is transient, the clear-dimming path (guarded by gridView.hasFocus() inside a postDelayed) may not run, leaving a row with several visibly greyed-out cards until the user interacts again.
rootCause: attachRowDimming() (~line 535-556) applies BrowseCardFocusHelper.applyNeighborDimming on focus-gain and only clears on focus-loss inside a 50ms postDelayed guarded by gridView.hasFocus() (lines 548-553). applyNeighborDimming (BrowseCardFocusHelper.kt:31-56) animates non-focused children to ALPHA_NEAR 0.65 / ALPHA_FAR 0.50. The effect is entirely focus-keyed (a 10-foot spotlight) and is NOT gated behind DeviceUtils.isTV — it runs on phones too, where focus is not the primary interaction model, so dimming can be applied without a reliable symmetric clear.
fix: Gate attachment to TV only: in attachRowDimming() wrap the applyNeighborDimming/highlightRowHeader/clearDimming wiring in if (DeviceUtils.isTV(requireContext())) so phones stay at full alpha — mirroring how presenters already gate GoldGlowFocusDrawable/FocusBracketDrawable behind DeviceUtils.isTV. This removes the sticky-dim risk entirely on touch.
correction: Confirmed: attachRowDimming (HomeFragment) is wired on every row's onBind with no isTV gate, and applyNeighborDimming/clearDimming (BrowseCardFocusHelper.kt) are not phone-gated. The clear path is guarded by gridView.hasFocus() in a postDelayed, which on touch (transient/absent focus) can skip, leaving residual dimming. P3 is correct (cosmetic). Minor note: the auditor cited 'lines 31-73' for BrowseCardFocusHelper; applyNeighborDimming is 31-56 and clearDimming is 61-73 — both relevant.

title: 3-panel side-by-side TV layout has no phone/portrait arrangement; panels collapse to unusable widths in portrait
symptom: On a phone in portrait, all three panels are laid out side-by-side at once: categories at 22% of width (~79dp on a 360dp phone), channels at 33% (~119dp), and preview+EPG at 45% (~162dp). Channel rows (48dp logo + 2-line name + EPG line + quality/country badges + favorite star) are crushed into a ~119dp column so names wrap/ellipsize hard and badges have almost no room; the EPG list is unreadable in its sliver; and nearly half the screen is donated to a video-preview frame that never plays on phone. The user sees three cramped columns instead of a single full-width channel list.
rootCause: Verified: there is exactly one layout file (app/src/main/res/layout/fragment_live_tv.xml) — no layout-television/ or layout-port/ variant of it exists (confirmed via find). Root content is a horizontal LinearLayout (lines 24-28) with three weighted children: categories_panel weight=22 (line 35), channels FrameLayout weight=33 (line 56), preview_panel weight=45 (line 79), each layout_height=match_parent with NO outer scroll. The only phone gating in onViewCreated (LiveTvFragment.kt lines 121-126) hides frosted_header and flips channelsList focusability/descendantFocusability — it never re-stacks the panels, never hides the preview, never widens the channel column. The 10-foot 3-column design renders verbatim on a portrait phone.
fix: Add a phone path in onViewCreated when !DeviceUtils.isTV(): set preview_panel visibility=GONE (it never runs on phone), and zero out the categories_panel layout_weight in favor of a top dropdown/chip strip OR set channels weight so the channel list takes the full remaining width. Cleanest is a layout-sw320dp/layout (or runtime ConstraintSet/weight swap) that stacks [category selector on top] over [full-width channels list] and drops the preview, optionally moving EPG into a bottom sheet. At minimum, reassign categories_panel/channels/preview_panel weights programmatically so channels is full-width on phone.

title: Entire header is set GONE on phone, making the in-screen channel search and MultiView entry point unreachable by touch
symptom: On a phone, the frosted header is hidden entirely. That header is the sole host of the channel-search icon/field and the MultiView icon on this screen, so a phone user on Live TV has no way to filter channels by name here and no touch affordance to launch MultiView from Live TV. The header_search_input filter that feeds updateCategoryList/updateChannelList is dead on phone.
rootCause: Verified: LiveTvFragment.kt line 122 unconditionally calls view.findViewById(R.id.frosted_header)?.visibility = View.GONE for any non-TV device. That header (fragment_live_tv.xml lines 180-272) is the only host of header_search_icon (242-256) and header_multiview_icon (258-271). The search toggle/filter wiring (lines 226-252) and the MultiView click (lines 217-219) are attached to those now-hidden views, so both are unreachable on phone with no replacement toolbar.
fix: Replace the blanket GONE with a phone-appropriate header: a slim Material toolbar exposing a 48dp search action and a MultiView/overflow action, or move both into a phone overflow/bottom-sheet. Do not leave the screen with zero in-screen search and no MultiView entry.
correction: Severity confirmed P1 (not P0): this is a degraded-but-usable screen, not unusable. Two factual corrections to the auditor's framing: (1) the header search is an IN-SCREEN channel-name FILTER (header_search_input -> searchFilter -> updateChannelList, lines 244-252), NOT the app's main Search screen — the global Search fragment is a separate top-level destination reachable from app nav, so phone users are not cut off from search entirely, only from filtering this channel list. (2) The MultiView icon is additionally gated by userPlanManager.isDeviceCapable() (line 200), so on many phones it would be GONE anyway; the lost touch entry only matters on capable devices. Both functions are still genuinely unreachable from Live TV on phone, so isReal=true stands.

title: Preview panel occupies 45% of phone width but never plays and is a focusable inert dead-zone on touch
symptom: On phone, ~45% of the horizontal space is the preview+EPG panel, but the muted preview NEVER starts (auto-preview is TV-only) so previewingChannel stays null. Tapping the preview area does nothing (the onClick is previewingChannel?.let { goFullscreen } — a no-op when null). Nearly half the screen is a static play-glyph placeholder that steals width from the already-cramped channel column and, being focusable in touch mode, can absorb a stray tap with no result.
rootCause: Verified: auto-preview is gated TV-only at line 356 (if (DeviceUtils.isTV() && !lowMemoryDevice)), so startPreviewFor is never scheduled on phone and previewingChannel stays null. previewContainer.isFocusable=true AND isFocusableInTouchMode=true are set UNCONDITIONALLY (lines 137-138) — not gated to TV. Its onClick (lines 139-141) is a no-op when previewingChannel==null. The 45%-weight preview_panel (fragment_live_tv.xml line 79) is never hidden on phone.
fix: On phone (!DeviceUtils.isTV()): set preview_panel visibility=GONE and reassign its weight to channels_list, since the preview has no function without auto-preview. Also guard previewContainer.isFocusable/isFocusableInTouchMode behind DeviceUtils.isTV() so it isn't a focusable dead target on touch. A single tap on a channel already goes straight to fullscreen (line 268 goFullscreen), so the preview concept can simply be dropped on phone.
correction: Minor refinement to the auditor's wording: the gold-glow focus OVERLAY on the preview IS already gated to TV (line 146, if (DeviceUtils.isTV())), so it won't paint on phone — but the auditor's core claim is still correct because isFocusable/isFocusableInTouchMode (lines 137-138) are NOT TV-gated, so the panel remains a focusable inert dead target on touch and still consumes 45% width. isReal=true stands.

title: Category list rows are 42dp tall (below 48dp Material minimum) in a ~79dp-wide column
symptom: Each category row is only 42dp tall and lives in the ~22%-width (~79dp) categories column, so on a phone the tappable target is both short (42dp < 48dp Material minimum) and narrow, with a 2dp inter-item margin — easy to mis-tap an adjacent category or spill into the channel column.
rootCause: Verified: item_category.xml line 5 hardcodes android:layout_height="42dp" with no phone override. card_category_height=72dp IS defined in values/dimens.xml line 14 but is NOT referenced by this layout (confirmed via grep — only one definition, no usage in item_category.xml). categories_panel is weight=22 (fragment_live_tv.xml line 35), a narrow column on phone.
fix: Bump the category row height to >=48dp for touch (e.g. a dedicated dimen referenced by item_category.xml with a values-television override keeping 42dp for D-pad density). Better, fold into the phone layout rework so categories become a horizontal chip strip / dropdown rather than a narrow vertical column.

title: Channel-card gold emphasis and real-EPG upgrade fire only on D-pad focus, not on touch
symptom: On a phone, finger-scrolling the channel list shows no selection/now-playing emphasis: the gold glow, 1.04x scale, gold accent bar, gold name tint, full-res logo swap, and the real-EPG + live-progress-bar upgrade for the focused row never appear, because all of these are driven by focus and touch scrolling does not move focus. An explicit tap launches fullscreen (no in-list selected state). The list looks less alive than on TV.
rootCause: Verified: all channel emphasis is inside root.setOnFocusChangeListener (ChannelPresenter.kt lines 109-161), and the real-EPG/progress upgrade keys off channelsList.selectedPosition / onChildViewHolderSelected (LiveTvFragment.kt lines 336-371 and 438-491) — i.e. D-pad focus events. On phone, channelsList is FOCUS_AFTER_DESCENDANTS + isFocusableInTouchMode=false (lines 124-125), so finger scrolling generates no focus change and none of the focus-gated visuals or the focused-row EPG refresh run.
fix: On phone, drive selected/now-playing visuals and the EPG upgrade from the center/visible item or from tap rather than focus — add an OnScrollListener (phone only) that picks the center-most channel, applies the emphasis, and calls the same EPG-upgrade path; or apply emphasis on ACTION_DOWN. The selectableItemBackground ripple on item_channel.xml line 12 already gives tap feedback.
correction: Severity corrected P2 -> P3 (polish, not friction). The auditor overstated 'the list reads as static/flat': verified that ChannelPresenter.onBindViewHolder (lines 78-87) binds an inferred 'on now' EPG line for EVERY row via epgResolver REGARDLESS of focus (the LiveTvFragment wires epgResolver at lines 176-180 with smartEpgFiller.inferRuleBased). So every channel row already shows name + an on-now blurb on phone; only the gold focus chrome and the real-EPG-vs-inferred UPGRADE for one row are missing. Channel name, logo, badges, favorite star, and an EPG line all render fine and the row taps through to fullscreen. This is cosmetic polish, not a usability defect — downgraded to P3. isReal=true stands (the focus-only visuals genuinely never fire on touch).

title: TV-only 25/75 horizontal split layout has no portrait/phone arrangement
symptom: On a phone in portrait the category sidebar is pinned to 25% of screen width (~90-100px on a typical 360dp-wide phone). Category names are heavily ellipsized (ellipsize=end, maxLines=1 at item_category.xml:39-40) and the in-sidebar count pill crowds the remaining width; the poster grid is squeezed into 75% of an already-narrow portrait width but does at least drop to 3 columns on phone (poster_columns=3 in values/dimens.xml:60 vs 4 on TV). It reads as a squashed TV screen, not a phone menu.
rootCause: fragment_vod.xml uses a single horizontal LinearLayout (lines 24-28) with android:layout_weight="25" on the sidebar (line 35) and android:layout_weight="75" on the VerticalGridView (line 70), both android:layout_height="match_parent". Confirmed there are only layout/ and layout-television/ resource dirs (no layout-port/, no layout-sw320dp/layout/), so portrait phones render this exact weighted split. The only phone adaptation in code is hiding nav hints + frosted header and a touch-passthrough fix on the poster grid (VodFragment.kt:81-87) — nothing re-weights or restructures the sidebar.
fix: Add a phone path. Either create res/layout-port/fragment_vod.xml that stacks a horizontal category strip (HorizontalGridView) above a full-width VerticalGridView, or in VodFragment.onViewCreated gate on !DeviceUtils.isTV() and re-set the vod_sidebar LinearLayout.LayoutParams weight (e.g. to ~38-40, or a fixed 130dp min width) so category names are legible. The 3-column phone grid already exists; the unsolved half is the cramped fixed-weight sidebar.
correction: Confirmed accurate. Verified: weights are exactly 25/75 (lines 35, 70), both match_parent height, only layout/ + layout-television/ exist (no portrait variant). One refinement to the auditor's symptom: the grid is NOT stuck at TV column counts — poster_columns is 3 on phone (values/dimens.xml:60) vs 4 on TV/sw600dp, so the poster side is less broken than implied; the real degradation is the ~90px ellipsized sidebar. Severity P1 is correct (badly degraded but usable — both panels still function and scroll).

title: Category RecyclerView missing the phone touch-passthrough treatment the poster grid gets
symptom: The category list's first finger tap can land on focus-acquisition instead of cleanly selecting, so the first tap on a category may visibly highlight/scale it (focus) rather than immediately switching the grid; a second tap then selects. The list DOES drag-scroll fine (plain RecyclerView claims the drag at touch slop). So this is mild first-tap friction, not a scroll break.
rootCause: The phone fix block (VodFragment.kt:81-87) applies FOCUS_AFTER_DESCENDANTS + isFocusableInTouchMode=false ONLY to posterGrid (lines 85-86). categoriesList (plain androidx.recyclerview.RecyclerView, LinearLayoutManager set at line 111) gets none of it, and every row in item_category.xml is focusable=true + focusableInTouchMode=true (lines 12-13). Verified CategoryListAdapter wires itemView.setOnClickListener at line 102, so tap-to-select DOES work — but the focusableInTouchMode rows plus the 60ms-debounced focus scale animation (CategoryListAdapter.kt:89-92) make the first touch register as a focus event with a visible 1.04x scale before the click is honored.
fix: In the !DeviceUtils.isTV() block, also set categoriesList.descendantFocusability = ViewGroup.FOCUS_AFTER_DESCENDANTS (mirroring posterGrid at lines 85-86) so a tap reaches the row click directly. Optionally also set categoriesList rows' focusableInTouchMode false on phone to suppress the focus-scale on first touch.
correction: Confirmed real but SEVERITY DOWNGRADED P2 -> P3. The auditor itself notes (and code confirms) the list scrolls fine and tap-to-select works via setOnClickListener (CategoryListAdapter.kt:102) — the only artifact is a cosmetic first-tap focus highlight/scale, which is polish, not noticeable functional friction. Category=scroll is acceptable since it sits in the scroll-passthrough family, though it is really a focus/touch artifact.

title: Category rows are 42dp tall — below the 48dp Material touch minimum
symptom: Category list rows on phone are 42dp tall (item_category.xml:5) plus a 2dp bottom margin (line 10), so the tappable height is under the 48dp Material minimum. Combined with the ~90px-wide portrait sidebar (finding vod-tv-2panel-no-portrait), categories are easy to mis-tap and fiddly to hit with a thumb.
rootCause: item_category.xml hard-codes android:layout_height="42dp" (line 5). Verified there is NO layout-television/item_category.xml override — the file is shared by phone and TV, so phone inherits the dense 42dp row. No values-sw320dp or other qualifier bumps it. The card_category_height dimen (72dp) exists in values/dimens.xml:14 but is unused by this layout.
fix: Make item_category.xml line 5 reference a dimen (e.g. @dimen/category_row_height) defined as >=48dp in values/ for phone, and add a 42dp override only in values-television/dimens.xml so the 10-foot UI keeps its density. (The auditor's suggestion to reuse @dimen/card_category_height=72dp would over-tall the row; 48-52dp is the right phone target.)
correction: Confirmed accurate. Verified 42dp literal at item_category.xml:5, 2dp bottom margin at line 10, no TV layout override of this item, card_category_height=72dp exists and is unused. Minor correction to the auditor's fix: reusing the 72dp card_category_height would make rows excessively tall; target ~48-52dp instead. Severity P2 correct.

title: VOD per-screen search is entirely hidden on phone (frosted_header GONE), plus the 28dp icon is sub-48dp on TV/tablet
symptom: On phone the entire frosted_header is set GONE (VodFragment.kt:83), and the only search entry point on the VOD screen — header_search_icon + header_search_input — lives inside that header. So a phone user has NO way to open the per-screen movie search/filter from the Movies tab; they must leave and use the global Search tab. The 28dp icon touch target (fragment_vod.xml:154-155, with 2dp padding = ~24dp glyph) is below 48dp, but that only matters on surfaces where the header is shown (TV/tablet).
rootCause: VodFragment.kt:83 hides frosted_header wholesale on !isTV. The header carries both decorative TV chrome (center logo, clock) AND the functional search affordance, so hiding the whole bar removes search on phone. header_search_icon is 28x28dp (fragment_vod.xml:154-155).
fix: Don't blanket-hide frosted_header on phone. Hide only the decorative children (header_center_logo, header_clock, header_logo) and keep header_search_icon + header_search_input visible, wrapping the icon in a >=48dp touch container. Alternatively, accept that VOD search is delegated to the bottom-nav Search tab and remove this as a defect — but currently the in-screen search simply vanishes with no replacement surfaced.
correction: Merged/recharacterized the auditor's vod-header-search-icon-target (was P3, confidence medium). The 28dp-target part is technically true but low-impact because the header is GONE on phone. The auditor buried the genuinely more serious issue in prose: hiding frosted_header (VodFragment.kt:83) removes the ONLY in-screen search entry point on phone. Promoted to the title and raised to P2 (functional loss, not polish). Verified: header_search_icon=28dp at fragment_vod.xml:154-155; frosted_header GONE at VodFragment.kt:83; search input/icon live only inside that header.

title: Poster long-press handler unconditionally returns true, lightly competing with drag-scroll
symptom: On phone, a slow press-and-hold on a poster at the start of a drag can pop the More Info overlay instead of scrolling, because the long-press fires and returns true. Minor — RecyclerView usually claims the drag at touch slop before the long-press timeout, so it only surfaces on a near-stationary slow finger-down.
rootCause: setOnLongClickListener (VodFragment.kt:152-166) returns true unconditionally (line 165), claiming the gesture with no check for in-progress scroll. The handler is attached to every poster on all device types (not gated to TV).
fix: Acceptable default Android behavior; if it annoys on phone, gate the long-press to !isPhone (it duplicates the tap->detail flow on touch, and the detail screen already exposes favorite/info), or guard it behind RecyclerView.SCROLL_STATE_IDLE before invoking the info overlay.
correction: Confirmed as a real but very minor (P3) issue, matching the auditor. Verified setOnLongClickListener returns true at line 165 with no scroll-state guard and no TV gating. Standard Android long-press-vs-scroll arbitration mostly resolves this in the user's favor, so impact is genuinely low.

title: [MISSED] Grid focus restore on back-nav uses grid.post{} — same race the v3.7.13 fix warned against
symptom: On returning to VOD from a movie detail (back navigation), the saved grid scroll/focus position is restored inside posterGrid.post{} (VodFragment.kt:240-246) on the skeleton->real-adapter swap. This posted restore can lose the race to leanback's deferred layout pass — the same failure mode the v3.7.13 fix explicitly called out and replaced with a SYNCHRONOUS selectedPosition write in updateMovieListInternal (lines 322-325). Worst case is a position-restore miss or, on slow devices, the historical 'Invalid item position -1' IOOBE family. Not a touch-drag-scroll break.
rootCause: Two different position-restore paths exist: updateMovieListInternal sets grid.selectedPosition SYNCHRONOUSLY after setItems (lines 322-325, the v3.7.13 hardening), but the skeleton-swap back-nav restore at lines 240-246 still uses posterGrid.post{ ... selectedPosition = ... }. The comment at lines 315-321 says synchronous is load-bearing precisely because a posted restore can be beaten by the layout pass.
fix: Move the savedGridPosition restore out of posterGrid.post{} and set posterGrid.selectedPosition synchronously right after assigning posterGrid.adapter = posterBridgeAdapter (line 238), bounds-coerced against posterAdapter.size()-1, consistent with the synchronous pattern in updateMovieListInternal.
correction: [MISSED] by the auditor. This is a real inconsistency with the project's own documented v3.7.13 invariant (CLAUDE.md: 'a grid.post{} restore loses the race; synchronous is load-bearing'). It is primarily a focus/restore correctness + slow-device crash-family concern rather than a touch-drag-scroll break on phone, hence P3 and category=scroll. Flagged for completeness; the touch-drag scrollability of the grid itself is unaffected and works (posterGrid passthrough at lines 85-86).

title: TV-only side-by-side category/grid split has no portrait phone arrangement

title: watchProgressMap setter does submitList(null)+submitList(current), collapsing the list to 0 height and jolting scroll on return from playback
symptom: After watching an episode and pressing back, the Series Detail page flickers and the scroll position resets — the user is bounced away from where they were in the episode list. On a long season this is a lose-my-place jolt every time they return from playback.
rootCause: EpisodeRecyclerAdapter.watchProgressMap is a custom setter (EpisodeRecyclerAdapter.kt:26-33) that calls submitList(null) then submitList(current). submitList(null) empties the ListAdapter to 0 items; because episodes_list is android:layout_height="wrap_content" with android:nestedScrollingEnabled="false" inside the NestedScrollView (fragment_series_detail.xml:186-198), the RecyclerView momentarily collapses to height 0, shrinking the scrollable content, then re-expands one frame later — the NestedScrollView clamps/repositions scrollY against the temporarily-shorter content. This setter runs on every onResume: SeriesDetailFragment.onResume() -> viewModel.refreshWatchProgress() (line 133) -> loadWatchProgress -> _episodeWatchProgress emits -> collectWatchProgress() (lines 285-289) reassigns watchProgressMap, executing the null/current round-trip even when the progress data is unchanged (the setter has no equality short-circuit).

In EpisodeRecyclerAdapter.kt:26-33, early-return when value == field, then rebind in place without going to 0 items: drop the `submitList(null)` line and instead `notifyItemRangeChanged(0, itemCount, PAYLOAD_PROGRESS)` (payload rebind) OR fold progress into Episode equality / areContentsTheSame and just `submitList(current.toList())`. Simplest stable-count fix: `if (field != value) { field = value; notifyItemRangeChanged(0, itemCount) }`.
correction: Confirmed as real and accurately described. The onResume -> refreshWatchProgress -> collectWatchProgress -> setter chain is verified (SeriesDetailFragment.kt:130-134, 285-289). The setter has no equality guard, so the null/current round-trip runs unconditionally. P1 correct.

title: Result rows use WRAP_CONTENT row height inside a vertical scroll parent — fragile leanback measure
symptom: Result HorizontalGridView rows are measured with WRAP_CONTENT for both the LayoutParams height and setRowHeight, which is a fragile leanback measure pattern; the codebase's own empty-state trending_row uses a fixed 260dp instead.

title: Grid/List toggle re-arms the staggered fade-in animation, making subsequent touch scrolling flash/fade rows
symptom: After tapping the Grid/List toggle, every favorite row that scrolls into view animates from alpha 0 -> 1 with a staggered start delay (pos*50ms, capped 500ms). On a phone, dragging the list after a view-mode switch makes freshly-recycled rows appear blank then fade in late, reading as laggy/broken scrolling — exactly the user's 'menus aren't scrolling properly' symptom.
rootCause: FavoritesAdapter.viewMode setter (lines 34-42) sets isFirstLoad=true and calls notifyDataSetChanged(). onViewAttachedToWindow (88-100), while isFirstLoad is true, sets itemView.alpha=0f and runs a delayed staggered fade-in on EVERY attaching holder. isFirstLoad is only cleared by markFirstLoadComplete() (102-104), which is called ONLY inside submitList's completion callback (FavoritesFragment.kt:263-264). Verified in the ViewModel: toggleViewMode() (134-136) flips only _viewMode and does NOT touch _allDisplayItems/_activeFilter/_sortMode, so the displayItems combine (69-80) does NOT re-emit on a toggle. submitList is therefore never re-invoked by the toggle, markFirstLoadComplete() never runs, and the per-item fade-in stays armed during all scrolling in the new mode.
fix: In the viewMode setter, do NOT set isFirstLoad=true (the user explicitly toggled — no entrance animation is needed), leaving isFirstLoad solely for genuine first data load. Alternatively, after notifyDataSetChanged() in the setter, post markFirstLoadComplete() to the next frame (focusHandler.post { isFirstLoad = false }) so only currently-visible items animate, OR gate onViewAttachedToWindow on a one-shot animatedPositions set so it never replays during ongoing scroll.
correction: CONFIRMED. One refinement to 'forever/indefinitely': the flag DOES self-heal on the next genuine displayItems emission — a filter-tab tap, sort change, favorite add/remove, or the unconditional 60s EPG refresh tick (FavoritesViewModel.kt:118-123 -> epgRefreshTrigger -> _allDisplayItems -> displayItems re-emit -> submitList -> markFirstLoadComplete). So the degraded-scroll window is bounded at up to ~60s, not truly permanent. The defect and P1 severity still stand: for the full window after a toggle, touch scrolling visibly flashes/fades rows, which is the exact complaint.

symptom: The horizontally-scrolling filter chips (All / Sports / Movies / etc.) are small targets on a phone — ~13sp text plus 6dp top/bottom padding (~30dp total height) — so tapping a specific category is fiddly and easy to miss.

They live in a HorizontalScrollView (fragment_favorites_aurora.xml:93-106) so horizontal scroll of the tab row is fine; the issue is purely per-tab tap size. Click wired at FavoritesFragment.kt:161 (selectFilterTab).
fix: When building each tab, on phone (DeviceUtils.isPhone) set tab.minimumHeight = (48*density).toInt() and increase vertical padding to ~12dp, or wrap each tab so its clickable bounds reach 48dp. Keep current compact sizing on TV.
correction: CONFIRMED. Code matches: 13f text, 6dp vertical padding, WRAP_CONTENT height, no minHeight. ~30dp total tap height is accurate and under the 48dp minimum.

title: Live Scores row uses a Leanback HorizontalGridView (touch-fling quirk) for sports favorites
symptom: When the user has live sports favorites with scores, a horizontal 'LIVE SCORES' strip appears. Because it's a Leanback HorizontalGridView (tuned for D-pad focus scrolling, not NestedScrollingChild), horizontal finger-fling can feel less smooth than a plain RecyclerView, and tapping a score card relies on a scroll+requestFocus pattern.
rootCause: scores_row is androidx.leanback.widget.HorizontalGridView (fragment_favorites_aurora.xml:142, height 64dp). The click handler (FavoritesFragment.kt:185-196) does favoritesGrid.scrollToPosition(pos) then requestFocus — a focus-driven pattern that is a no-op for focus on touch but the scroll still works. Non-blocking: the strip only appears for the sports/all filter when score items exist (updateScoresBar, FavoritesFragment.kt:327-344).
fix: For the phone path, swap scores_row to a plain androidx.recyclerview.widget.RecyclerView with a horizontal LinearLayoutManager for natural touch fling, or leave as-is on TV. Low priority since the row is conditionally shown and not part of the main vertical scroll.
correction: CONFIRMED as a genuine-but-minor polish item, P3 is correct. Important clarification the auditor was right about: this HorizontalGridView is a SIBLING above the main RecyclerView (inside scores_bar_container in the vertical LinearLayout), NOT nested inside a NestedScrollView and NOT the main vertical list — so it does NOT block or steal the page's vertical drag-scroll. The defect is limited to horizontal-fling smoothness within the 64dp strip itself.

title: Read-only dashboard forces a 3-column horizontal card row on phones with no portrait variant
symptom: On a phone the three cards (Account info / Subscription days / Connections) are crammed side-by-side into one screen width. With outer overscan padding of 12dp/side (values/dimens.xml) and two 16dp inter-card margins, on a 360dp phone each weighted card is only ~100dp wide; after each card's 24dp x2 = 48dp internal padding, ~50-53dp of usable width remains. The 72sp days-remaining number, the 'days remaining' label, the server URL, and the gauge are squeezed, wrapped, or clipped. It reads as broken/cramped, not a phone dashboard.
rootCause: content_area is hardcoded android:orientation="horizontal" (line 38) with three children each android:layout_weight="1" (lines 42-49, 137-145, 185-192). Verified there is only one layout file: layout/fragment_account_dashboard.xml (find returned no layout-port/, no phone-specific variant; only layout/ and layout-television/ exist, and the TV variant does not include this file). AccountDashboardFragment never branches on DeviceUtils.isPhone()/isTV() (grep of the whole account/ package returned zero device gating and zero orientation manipulation). The 3-up arrangement only makes sense at 10-foot/landscape TV width.
fix: Stack the cards vertically on phones. Cleanest: set the content_area LinearLayout to android:orientation="vertical" in the base layout/ XML (each card layout_width=match_parent, layout_weight=0, swap layout_marginEnd->layout_marginBottom) and keep horizontal only in a new layout-television/fragment_account_dashboard.xml. Alternatively, in onViewCreated do: if (DeviceUtils.isPhone(requireContext())) { contentArea.orientation = LinearLayout.VERTICAL; for each card set layoutParams.width = MATCH_PARENT, weight = 0f }. Vertical stacking lets the existing ScrollView scroll the cards naturally.
correction: Confirmed real, severity P1 correct. Minor inaccuracy in the auditor's summary/symptom: the '48dp internal padding' is the per-card 24dpx2, NOT the outer page padding. The outer overscan_horizontal is 12dp on phones (values/dimens.xml), not 48dp (48dp is values-television only). Real per-card width is ~100dp, not the auditor's ~112dp, with ~50-53dp usable, not ~64dp. The defect itself stands exactly as described. Line citation 34-220 corrected to specific lines 38/42-49/137-145/185-192.

title: ConnectionGaugeView fixed at 140dp x 140dp overflows the ~100dp phone column
symptom: On a phone the circular connections gauge is declared 140dp wide but lives in a weighted column only ~100dp wide (~50dp after the card's 24dp x2 padding). The right card visibly overflows/clips the gauge and the '<active>/<max>' center text; the right edge of the gauge is cut off by the card background.
rootCause: The gauge has fixed android:layout_width="140dp" android:layout_height="140dp" (lines 206-207). Because the dimension is fixed, the parent passes an EXACTLY=140dp MeasureSpec, so ConnectionGaugeView.onMeasure (lines 69-76) computes minOf(140,140)=140 and calls setMeasuredDimension(140,140) regardless of the ~100dp column width -> the view measures larger than its slot and overflows/clips. No values-sw320dp/values-sw600dp override exists for this size and there is no responsive sizing.
fix: Primary fix is the vertical stack (account-3col-horizontal-no-portrait), after which the column is full-width and 140dp fits. Defense-in-depth: extract @dimen/connection_gauge_size (140dp in values/, e.g. 120dp in values-sw320dp/dimens.xml) and reference it from the XML so onMeasure (which already clamps to a square) adapts. Note: making it wrap_content alone will NOT help because onMeasure ignores the incoming mode and forces a square from the spec SIZE; the real lever is the layout_width value / a responsive dimen.
correction: Confirmed real, severity P1 correct, onMeasure citation (lines 69-76) accurate. Correction: column is ~100dp not ~112dp. Also clarified the onMeasure mechanism: with a FIXED 140dp layout_width the child receives an EXACTLY spec of 140, so it always measures 140 and overflows; the auditor's 'still tries to honor 140dp' is right but the fix note that onMeasure 'will adapt to whatever width the stacked card gives it' is only true once layout_width stops being a hardcoded 140dp -- onMeasure does not currently respect the incoming constraint, it derives size purely from the spec SIZE values.

title: No on-screen back button - phone users rely solely on the system back gesture to leave the dashboard
symptom: After opening Account Dashboard from Settings, a touch user sees a full-screen 'Account Dashboard' header (TextView at lines 15-22) with no back arrow. They can only return via the OS back gesture/button; there is no in-screen touch affordance to go back.
rootCause: Navigated via supportFragmentManager.beginTransaction().replace(R.id.main_container, fragment).addToBackStack(null).commit() (SettingsFragment.navigateToFragment, lines 353-358) so system Back DOES pop it (reachability intact). But the layout has only a static title TextView, no toolbar/back button, and no PhoneToolbarHelper is applied in AccountDashboardFragment (unlike VodDetail/SeriesDetail which got phone back-arrows in v3.7.11). Consistency/polish gap, not a hard blocker.
fix: Add a phone-only back affordance consistent with the app: apply the existing common/PhoneToolbarHelper (gradient scrim + circular back button) in onViewCreated when DeviceUtils.isPhone(), wired to requireActivity().onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed(). Gate off on TV (D-pad back handles it).
correction: Confirmed real, severity P3 correct. navigateToFragment verified at SettingsFragment.kt:353-358 (replace + addToBackStack(null) + commit). Action dispatch confirmed at line 239 (ACTION_ACCOUNT). Layout confirmed to have no back/toolbar widget. Auditor accurate on all points.

title: PIN entry is a Leanback GuidedStepSupportFragment — the only gateway into Parental Settings, and it is a TV D-pad UI on phones
symptom: On a phone, Settings > Parental Controls lands the user in a full-screen Leanback two-pane guidance UI (title/description pane + vertical actions list) with 10-foot type, large left margins, and a focus/highlight model built for a remote. The PIN field is a GuidedAction with descriptionEditable=true (ParentalPinFragment.kt:99-104); the IME does come up when tapped, but advancing from the PIN field to the Unlock action relies on onGuidedActionEditedAndProceed returning ACTION_ID_NEXT (line 171-175), a D-pad navigation concept with no touch-native equivalent. This is the sole entry point to every parental setting (SettingsFragment.kt:240 navigateToFragment(ParentalPinFragment())).
rootCause: ParentalPinFragment extends androidx.leanback.app.GuidedStepSupportFragment (line 22) with zero DeviceUtils.isPhone() gating and no phone alternative (verified: no isPhone/isTV references anywhere in the parental package). SettingsFragment is itself a GuidedStepSupportFragment (SettingsFragment.kt:35) and launches it directly at line 240. There are no layout-port/ or phone-variant resources — phones render the TV GuidedStep chrome.
fix: Gate on DeviceUtils.isPhone(): branch in SettingsFragment.onGuidedActionClicked ACTION_PARENTAL (line 240) to present a Material AlertDialog/BottomSheet PIN entry (EditText inputType=numberPassword + Unlock/Cancel) on phone instead of navigateToFragment(ParentalPinFragment()); keep the GuidedStep path only for isTV(). Same treatment for the Change-PIN entry launched from ParentalSettingsFragment.setupQuickActions (line 88-96).
correction: Confirmed exactly as described. Files cited correctly; verified ParentalPinFragment.kt:22 extends GuidedStepSupportFragment, the editable PIN GuidedActions, the ACTION_ID_NEXT D-pad advance at line 174, and SettingsFragment.kt:240 as the sole entry. One nuance the auditor under-weighted: the Change-PIN flow (ParentalSettingsFragment.kt:88-96) also re-enters this same GuidedStep fragment, so the TV-shaped PIN UI is hit on a second path too. Severity P1 is correct — it is usable on touch (IME works, fields are tappable) but badly TV-shaped, not fully broken.

title: Quick-action buttons row is wrap_content + centered + non-scrolling — overflows/clips on narrow phones
symptom: The bottom action row (lines 114-159) holds three wrap_content buttons — 'Block All Adult', 'Allow All', 'Change PIN' — each with 16dp+16dp internal padding and 12dp inter-button margins, in a horizontal LinearLayout with gravity=center and no HorizontalScrollView. Estimated intrinsic width ~320dp. With the root LinearLayout's android:padding=48dp (line 8) consuming 96dp, available width is ~264dp on a 360dp phone and ~224dp on a 320dp phone — so the row overflows and gets clipped. Because gravity=center, BOTH outer buttons ('Block All Adult' on the left and 'Change PIN' on the right) are cut off at the edges, and there is no horizontal scroll to reach them, so the user cannot fully tap the clipped actions.
rootCause: fragment_parental_settings.xml lines 114-159: three android:layout_width=wrap_content buttons in a single non-wrapping, non-scrolling gravity=center horizontal LinearLayout. The drawables (bg_action_button_red/green/gold) carry no min-width, so width is pure intrinsic content. The outer 48dp root padding (line 8) is a TV overscan value applied identically to phones, stealing ~96dp before any content.
fix: Make the buttons reflow: set each to android:layout_width=0dp android:layout_weight=1 and drop gravity=center (equal thirds), or wrap the row in a FlexboxLayout / stack to two rows on narrow widths. Also replace android:padding=48dp on the root (line 8) with @dimen/overscan_horizontal (12dp phone / 8dp sw320dp / 48dp values-television) so phones recover ~84-88dp of width — this dimen already exists in the project.
correction: Confirmed real. Correction to the auditor's description: the container uses android:gravity="center" (line 119), so on overflow the clipping is SYMMETRIC — both the leftmost ('Block All Adult') and rightmost ('Change PIN') buttons are cut, not just the rightmost as the auditor claimed. Severity P1 retained because a center-clipped non-scrolling row can leave a primary action (Change PIN / Block All Adult) partially or fully unreachable on a 320-360dp phone. The fix correctly leans on the already-existing @dimen/overscan_horizontal (verified: 48dp TV / 12dp default / 8dp sw320dp), which this layout does not use.

title: Category rows + tabs set focusableInTouchMode=true — TV-only attribute that hurts touch scroll/fling, not a double-tap toggle bug
symptom: Each category row is android:focusable=true android:focusableInTouchMode=true (item_category_toggle.xml:10-11) and so are all three tab TextViews (fragment_parental_settings.xml:65-66, 79-80, 92-93). focusableInTouchMode on RecyclerView list items makes the framework try to retain a focused child during touch scroll/fling, which can cause minor scroll jank and unexpected auto-scroll-to-focused behavior on phone. It is a TV-only attribute that has no benefit on touch.
rootCause: item_category_toggle.xml:10-11 and the tab TextViews hardcode focusableInTouchMode=true for D-pad/TV focus. The toggle Switch is correctly focusable=false/clickable=false (lines 19-20) and the row click toggles via bindingAdapterPosition (CategoryToggleAdapter.kt:34-39), so toggling itself works on a single tap.
fix: Remove android:focusableInTouchMode=true from item_category_toggle.xml (keep android:focusable for D-pad) and from the three tab TextViews, or set it conditionally for TV only via a values-television style. Add android:foreground=?android:attr/selectableItemBackground to the row for a visible touch ripple.
correction: Real that the attribute is TV-only and inappropriate on phone rows, BUT the auditor's headline symptom ('first tap grabs focus instead of firing the click, user must tap twice to toggle') is wrong. In Android touch mode a tap on a clickable view fires its OnClickListener on the first tap regardless of focusableInTouchMode — the double-tap pathology is specific to EditText/IME widgets, not a plain clickable row with a click listener (CategoryToggleAdapter.kt:34-39 fires on first tap). The genuine, lower-grade concern is focus-retention jank during fling. Downgraded confidence to low and re-scoped the symptom; severity P2 retained but it is closer to polish than friction.

title: fragment_parental_settings.xml is a single TV-derived layout (48dp overscan padding, 24dp row insets) with no phone variant
symptom: On a phone the screen wastes scarce width: the root LinearLayout has android:padding=48dp on all sides (line 8 — a 10-foot overscan margin, ~96dp horizontal + ~96dp vertical lost) and each list row has android:paddingStart/End=24dp (item_category_toggle.xml:8-9). Category names get squeezed into a narrow central column and long names truncate, with large empty borders — visibly a TV layout on a phone. The list itself still scrolls fine; this is density/whitespace degradation, not a scroll break.
rootCause: Only one layout/ variant exists for this screen (no layout-port/ or sw-qualified layout) and the paddings are hardcoded dp instead of referencing the project's existing @dimen/overscan_horizontal (12dp phone / 8dp sw320dp / 48dp values-television). The 48dp root padding and 24dp row insets are TV overscan values applied identically to phones.
fix: Replace android:padding=48dp on the root (line 8) with @dimen/overscan_horizontal for horizontal and a small/zero vertical dimen, and replace the 24dp paddingStart/End in item_category_toggle.xml (lines 8-9) with @dimen/spacing_md (16dp) or a phone-appropriate dimen. This reuses the existing values-television override pattern already used elsewhere in the app.
correction: Confirmed exactly. Verified the hardcoded 48dp root padding (line 8) and 24dp row insets (item_category_toggle.xml:8-9), and confirmed the @dimen/overscan_horizontal token already exists at 48dp(TV)/12dp(default)/8dp(sw320dp) but is NOT referenced by this layout. Severity P2 correct — degraded density, list still scrolls.

title: No on-screen back/up affordance — phone user relies on system Back only; PhoneToolbarHelper pattern not applied here
symptom: fragment_parental_settings.xml has a header row ('Parental Controls' + ON status, lines 10-35) but no visible back arrow / up button, so a phone user can only leave via system Back. After unlock, ParentalPinFragment.navigateToSettings() (lines 328-338) pops the PIN fragment then replaces with ParentalSettingsFragment + addToBackStack(null); returning lands on the GuidedStep Settings screen. Reachability works via system Back, but there is no touch-native toolbar/back control like the rest of the phone overhaul.

Low priority — system Back already works.
correction: Confirmed. Verified the header layout has no back view, the navigateToSettings pop/replace logic (lines 328-338), and that PhoneToolbarHelper.attach exists and is wired into VodDetailFragment + SeriesDetailFragment but not the parental screens. P3 is correct since system Back is functional; this is a consistency/polish gap.

title: [MISSED] Quick-action buttons (40dp) and section tabs (44dp) are below the 48dp Material touch-target minimum
symptom: The three Quick-Action buttons are android:layout_height=40dp (lines 125, 138, 151) and the three section tabs are android:layout_height=44dp (lines 56, 71, 85), both under the 48dp Material/Android touch-target minimum. On a phone these are finger-tapped, so the slightly short targets are marginally harder to hit accurately, especially combined with the overflow clipping on the button row.
rootCause: Heights hardcoded at TV-comfortable sizes (40dp/44dp) where D-pad focus makes target size irrelevant; never bumped to 48dp for the touch build, and no values-television override to keep them compact on TV while enlarging on phone.

Pair this with the layout-weight reflow fix from parental-quick-actions-overflow so the buttons are both reachable and tall enough.
correction: [MISSED] The auditor flagged focusableInTouchMode and the button overflow but did not separately call out that the action buttons (40dp) and tabs (44dp) fall short of the 48dp touch-target minimum. Verified heights at fragment_parental_settings.xml lines 56/71/85 (tabs=44dp) and 125/138/151 (buttons=40dp). Minor (P3) — within a few dp of the minimum — but a legitimate touch-target miss on the phone build. Note: the 56dp category rows and the row-as-target pattern for the toggle ARE correct and meet the minimum.

title: Content column hard-coded to 400dp width clips on small/narrow phones
symptom: On a small/narrow phone (~320dp wide), the centered Speed Test column is wider than the usable screen (320dp - 2*8dp overscan = ~304dp). The left/right edges of the column overflow and are clipped by the non-scrolling FrameLayout. The progress bar and Run Test button are layout_width=match_parent so they size to the 400dp parent and lose ~48dp off each side. The button's centered 'Run Test' text and the bulk of its tap area stay on-screen and remain tappable, so the screen is still usable; the defect is the edges looking truncated/broken, not loss of function.
rootCause: fragment_speed_test.xml line 9: the inner LinearLayout uses a fixed android:layout_width="400dp" inside a FrameLayout (line 2-6) with layout_gravity="center". 400dp exceeds usable width on sw320dp (~304dp) and 360dp (~336dp) phones. FrameLayout does not scroll horizontally, so overflow is clipped. progress_bar (line 64) and run_test_button (line 84) are match_parent and inherit the 400dp width.
fix: Change line 9 from android:layout_width="400dp" to android:layout_width="match_parent" and add android:layout_marginHorizontal="24dp" (and optionally keep the 400dp look on tablets/TV via a @dimen reference defined per qualifier). Since the content is just stacked centered text plus one full-width button, match_parent with horizontal margins always fits and keeps the button/progress bar within screen bounds.
correction: Confirmed the 400dp overflow on narrow phones. Severity downgraded P1 -> P2: nothing becomes non-functional. The button text 'Run Test' is centered and its tap area stays on-screen even when the ~400dp button overflows; there is no list to lose access to. This is cosmetic edge-clipping / friction, not a badly-degraded-but-usable screen-level break. Also corrected the citation: the dimens are inherited via match_parent children, not separate overriding dimens; values-sw320dp/dimens.xml line 4 only changes overscan_margin (8dp), it does NOT define a speed-test card width, so the auditor's suggestion to add a per-qualifier dimen is valid but the file as-cited contains no card-width dimen.

title: No on-screen back affordance; relies on system/gesture Back only
symptom: A phone user opening Speed Test from Settings sees no visible back arrow or close button. To leave they must use system/gesture Back. It works (added to back stack) but there is no in-app touch affordance.

fix: On phone only (DeviceUtils.isPhone()), overlay a small circular back button via PhoneToolbarHelper that calls requireActivity().onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed(). TV path unchanged. Low priority since gesture Back works.
correction: Confirmed as-is. Verified SettingsFragment.kt lines 353-358 match (replace + addToBackStack(null) + commit) and fragment_speed_test.xml has no back affordance. P3 is correct. Note: SpeedTestFragment.onKeyEvent always returns false (line 121), so it does not intercept the D-pad/Back key — back is handled by the activity's normal back-stack pop, which gesture Back also triggers, so the path genuinely works on touch.

title: Settings is a TV-only side-by-side GuidedStep two-pane layout with no phone/portrait path — guidance pane eats ~58% of width, the menu is jammed into ~42%
symptom: On a phone in portrait the Settings screen renders exactly as on a 10-foot TV: the 'Settings / Manage your Ooustream account and preferences' title block occupies the LEFT ~58% of the screen as a fixed pane while the entire actionable menu (Account, Parental Controls, Subtitle Settings, Backup, Speed Test, etc.) is squeezed into the RIGHT ~42% column. Row titles/descriptions wrap and feel cramped; there is no full-width vertical list a phone user expects.
rootCause: Verified: SettingsFragment.kt:35, SubtitleSettingsFragment.kt:15, SettingsConfirmFragment.kt:13 all extend androidx.leanback.app.GuidedStepSupportFragment with zero DeviceUtils.isPhone()/isTV() gating anywhere in the settings package (grep returned NONE). App theme is parent="Theme.Leanback" (themes.xml:3) with no GuidanceStylist/GuidedActionsStylist/onProvideTheme override. The stock leanback-1.0.0 lb_guidedstep_fragment.xml (verified from the extracted AAR) lays out content_frame as a HORIZONTAL LinearLayout (line 35): content_fragment (guidance) at layout_weight=1, action_fragment_root at layout_weight=?attr/guidedActionContentWidthWeight. Verified value lb_guidedactions_width_weight=0.71428571428 (values.xml:753) → guidance 1/1.714≈58.3%, actions 0.714/1.714≈41.7%. guidedStepHeightWeight=2.0 of weightSum=2 fills the full screen. Only layout/ and layout-television/ resource dirs exist — no layout-port/layout-sw320dp variant.
