Gate on DeviceUtils.isPhone(requireContext()) at the Settings entry points (MainActivity.kt:234 'settings' -> SettingsFragment(); HomeFragment.kt:1901). On phone, render a full-width vertical androidx.recyclerview.RecyclerView (LinearLayoutManager) of settings rows in a normal Fragment with a Material toolbar + back arrow (reuse PhoneToolbarHelper from v3.7.11), or a BottomSheetDialogFragment list following the established PhoneTrackPickerSheet/PhoneContentInfoSheet pattern. Keep the GuidedStep path for isTV(). This is the deferred work noted in CLAUDE.md ('Deferred to v3.7.12: GuidedStepSupportFragment phone replacements (Settings...)').
correction: Confirmed as-is. Minor cited-line nit: the auditor pinned exact lines (SettingsFragment.kt:35 etc.) which are the class declarations — correct. Navigation entries MainActivity.kt:234 and HomeFragment.kt:1901 also verified accurate.

title: Settings menu is a focus-tuned Leanback VerticalGridView — finger drag DOES scroll, but tapping a row snaps it to the keyline (jarring), and the cramped ~42% width hurts more than the scroll mechanics
symptom: Verified actual behavior: a finger drag/fling DOES scroll the actions list (it is a normal RecyclerView at its core), so the bottom 'Logout' item is reachable by dragging. The real friction is that on a TAP, the tapped row gains focus and the list re-aligns/snaps that row to the fixed ~40%-from-top keyline (focusScrollStrategy=FOCUS_SCROLL_ALIGNED), which feels like the list 'jumps' under the finger. Combined with the menu being squeezed into ~42% of portrait width, the experience is awkward — but it is NOT 'unscrollable / cannot reach the bottom'.
rootCause: The actions list IS androidx.leanback.widget.VerticalGridView (id=guidedactions_list, verified in extracted lb_guidedactions.xml lines 42-45) with style Widget.Leanback.GuidedActionsListStyle (values.xml:1421): focusable=false, focusableInTouchMode=false, layout_height=match_parent (NOT wrap_content — so it fills the pane and is the genuine scroll container; there is NO outer ScrollView, so NO nested-scroll conflict). Decompiled BaseGridView.class constant pool: NO 'NestedScroll*' tokens (so the auditor is right it lacks NestedScrollingChild) BUT also NO onTouchEvent override and NO suppressLayout/setLayoutFrozen — it inherits RecyclerView.onTouchEvent, which performs standard drag/fling scrolling. GridLayoutManager.class exposes canScrollVertically + scrollVerticallyBy + smoothScrollBy. Therefore touch drag-scroll works. SettingsFragment.onCreateActions adds 15 actions (verified: 15 GuidedAction.Builder calls, not 16 — the 'Reset Playback Recovery' action was removed in v3.7.0, see comment at line 199-200). lb_guidedstep_keyline=40.0 (values.xml:758) is the focus-alignment keyline, confirmed.
fix: Resolved by the phone replacement list in settings-guidedstep-no-portrait-twopane: a plain RecyclerView + LinearLayoutManager scrolls naturally on touch with no keyline-snap and at full width. Do NOT wrap the GuidedStep in a ScrollView (that WOULD create a nested-scroll conflict). No standalone P0 fix is warranted because the grid is not actually unscrollable.
correction: Auditor OVERSTATED this. (1) Severity P0->P2: the list IS drag-scrollable on touch (RecyclerView onTouchEvent inherited; GridLayoutManager.scrollVerticallyBy/canScrollVertically present; match_parent height, no outer scroll parent = no nested-scroll conflict). The 'cannot reliably scroll to the bottom / Logout unreachable by drag' claim is the exact type-(b) mistake (calling a working RecyclerView 'can't scroll'). (2) Action count is 15, not 16. (3) The genuine residual friction (keyline focus-snap on tap + 42% width crunch) overlaps with the layout P0, so this is not an independent P0 scroll defect.

title: Guidance/title pane is a fixed non-scrollable pane that permanently steals ~58% of portrait width from the menu
symptom: The left guidance column ('Settings' + 'Manage your Ooustream account and preferences') is dead, non-interactive space on a phone — it never scrolls, never collapses, and consumes ~58% of portrait width while the real menu is choked into the remainder. On SettingsConfirmFragment the same waste applies to a simple Confirm/Cancel screen.
rootCause: Verified: onCreateGuidance() in all three fragments returns a GuidanceStylist.Guidance (SettingsFragment.kt:63-70, SubtitleSettingsFragment.kt:28-35, SettingsConfirmFragment.kt:15-22). The stock lb_guidance.xml (extracted) is a FrameLayout containing a GuidanceStylingRelativeLayout of TextViews (icon/breadcrumb/title/description) with NO ScrollView — a fixed 10-foot title pane. In the horizontal content_frame it is pinned at layout_weight=1 (~58% width, match_parent height). There is no phone arrangement that stacks guidance above a full-width list.
fix: In the phone replacement screen, drop the guidance pane entirely (or render the title as a compact top app-bar header) and give 100% width to the vertical settings list — resolved automatically by implementing the phone RecyclerView/BottomSheet replacement in settings-guidedstep-no-portrait-twopane.
correction: Confirmed as-is, though this is effectively the same root defect as settings-guidedstep-no-portrait-twopane (the 58/42 split is one horizontal LinearLayout). Kept as a distinct P1 facet because it specifically flags the guidance pane's non-scrollable wasted width; both are fixed by the single phone-replacement change.

title: Settings action rows have no enforced 48dp minimum touch height — TV-density rows can fall below Material minimum on phone
symptom: On a phone, single-line settings rows (e.g. SubtitleSettings 'Auto-Enable Subtitles' = 'On', or 'About') are short and tightly packed, making them easy to mis-tap or to hit the adjacent row when tapping after a scroll.
rootCause: Verified: the GuidedStep item container is androidx.leanback.widget.GuidedActionItemContainer (extracted lb_guidedactions_item.xml) styled via ?attr/guidedActionItemContainerStyle. The app defines no override for that style in res/values (grep found none), so rows inherit the TV-tuned container whose height is driven by title/description text metrics + small paddings with NO android:minHeight=48dp. values/dimens.xml and values-sw320dp/dimens.xml define no guided-action row height. Row height is therefore not pinned to the Material 48dp touch-target minimum on phone.
fix: Resolved by the phone replacement list: size each phone settings row to minHeight=48dp (ideally 56dp list-item height). If an interim TV-shared tweak is wanted, add a Widget.Leanback.GuidedActionItemContainerStyle override with android:minHeight="48dp" in res/values — but the proper fix is the phone list.
correction: Confirmed plausible. Could not measure the exact rendered pixel height of a single-line row from static resources alone (it depends on text metrics + the inherited style's paddings, which resolve at runtime), hence medium confidence — but the absence of any minHeight override is verified, so rows are NOT guaranteed >=48dp. Severity P2 is correct (friction, not blocking).

title: SettingsConfirmFragment / sub-screens have no in-screen touch back arrow — dismiss relies on system/gesture back (but Cancel button and back gesture both work)
symptom: Clear Cache and Logout push a full-screen GuidedStep confirm (SettingsConfirmFragment) with Confirm/Cancel actions in the cramped right pane; sub-navigations (Account, Parental, Subtitle, Backup, Speed Test, Update) are pushed via supportFragmentManager.replace + addToBackStack with no in-screen back arrow. A phone user must use the system/gesture back to return — there is no on-screen back affordance in the Settings flow itself.
rootCause: Verified: SettingsConfirmFragment is GuidedStepSupportFragment-based and dismisses via parentFragmentManager.popBackStack() (lines 43, 46) with no toolbar/back button. navigateToFragment (SettingsFragment.kt:353-358) does replace(R.id.main_container) + addToBackStack(null) with no back UI. Reachability of BACK is fine: MainActivity overrides onBackPressed() (line 250) and the global back dispatcher pops the stack, and each confirm screen has an explicit tappable 'Cancel' guided action. So the user is NOT stranded.
fix: When the settings flow is reimplemented for phone, give confirm dialogs a real Material android.app.AlertDialog (the codebase already uses it for Clear History at SettingsFragment.kt:448-458 — make Clear Cache and Logout consistent instead of GuidedStep confirms) and add a touch back affordance to each pushed sub-screen (reuse PhoneToolbarHelper from v3.7.11).
correction: Severity DOWNGRADED P2->P3. The auditor framed this near a reachability risk, but verification shows return is fully reachable on touch: MainActivity.onBackPressed() + global back gesture pops the stack, and confirm screens expose a tappable Cancel action. So it is polish/consistency (no native-feeling back arrow, GuidedStep confirm instead of AlertDialog), not a real navigation dead-end.

title: [MISSED] SettingsConfirmFragment stores the onConfirm callback in a companion (static) field — process-death / config recreation drops or cross-wires the confirm action
symptom: Not a touch/scroll defect per the user complaint, but a correctness foot-gun adjacent to the confirm flow: if the Clear-Cache or Logout confirm screen is recreated by the system (process death while backgrounded), or if two confirm screens are ever opened in sequence, the tapped 'Confirm' may invoke the wrong action or no action, because the callback isn't part of the saved fragment state.
rootCause: Verified: SettingsConfirmFragment.newInstance() assigns onConfirm to a companion-object var onConfirmCallback (lines 63, 71). It is a single static slot, not retained via arguments or a ViewModel. After process death the static is null on restore (Confirm does nothing); if a second confirm is created it overwrites the first's callback. MainActivity sets configChanges to avoid recreation on rotation, which masks this in the common case, but it is still fragile. The class comment even notes it mirrors ClearConfirmFragment's pattern — so the same issue may exist there.
fix: Replace the GuidedStep confirms with android.app.AlertDialog (already the pattern for Clear History at SettingsFragment.kt:448) so the callback lives in the calling fragment's scope, OR route the result via a Fragment Result API (setFragmentResult/setFragmentResultListener) / shared ViewModel keyed by an action id, so the confirm survives recreation. This naturally folds into the phone-replacement work.
correction: [MISSED] by the auditor. Flagged as low-severity (P3) because it is a correctness/lifecycle issue, not the touch-scroll problem the user reported; included for completeness since it sits directly in the Settings confirm path the auditor was reviewing.

title: GuidedStep actions list is a focus-aligned VerticalGridView — finger scroll re-aligns to focus, but lists here all fit on screen
symptom: On a phone the guided actions render in a Leanback VerticalGridView (lb_guidedactions.xml id guidedactions_list). Finger drag DOES move the list (RecyclerView touch path is intact), but the grid re-aligns scroll to the focused row, so a flick that lands focus elsewhere snaps the list back. In practice this is invisible on these three screens because every list fits on a phone screen: Update has exactly 2 actions (UpdateFragment.kt:44-58), ClearConfirm has 2 (ClearConfirmFragment.kt:20-31), Backup has 4 short rows (BackupFragment.kt:31-63). There is no overflow to scroll, so 'can't reach Clear All Data' does not actually occur in portrait on a normal phone.
rootCause: All three extend androidx.leanback.app.GuidedStepSupportFragment (UpdateFragment.kt:17, BackupFragment.kt:17, ClearConfirmFragment.kt:8). The actions pane is a Leanback VerticalGridView styled by guidedActionsListStyle (verified in leanback-1.0.0.aar res/layout/lb_guidedactions.xml line 42-45). VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIBRARY: leanback GridLayoutManager overrides canScrollVertically() and scrollVerticallyBy() and has setScrollEnabled(true) by default, and BaseGridView.dispatchTouchEvent only intercepts when an OnTouchInterceptListener is set (none is set here) — otherwise it delegates straight to RecyclerView.dispatchTouchEvent. So the list IS touch-scrollable; the only quirk is focus-aligned re-snap, not a hard scroll lock. The theme is Theme.Ooustream which has parent="Theme.Leanback" (themes.xml:3).
fix: Low urgency since these lists never overflow on phone. The correct long-term fix is to gate on DeviceUtils.isPhone() (common/DeviceUtils.kt) and present a plain RecyclerView/LinearLayoutManager (or AlertDialog for ClearConfirm) on phone, only using GuidedStep when DeviceUtils.isTV(). If kept as GuidedStep, no scroll-specific change is needed for these three because content fits; do NOT claim the list is unscrollable.
correction: Severity downgraded P1 -> P3 and the mechanism claim corrected. The auditor wrote 'Leanback grids do not implement NestedScrollingChild correctly, so free touch panning is not provided' and 'a drag either snaps the list back to the focused item or barely moves; the list feels stuck.' That is an overstatement of the bug. Decompiling leanback-1.0.0.aar shows GridLayoutManager DOES override scrollVerticallyBy()/canScrollVertically() and BaseGridView.dispatchTouchEvent does NOT intercept touch unless an (unset) listener exists — so finger drag scrolls the list normally; it merely re-aligns to focus. More importantly, all three screens' action lists fit on a phone screen (2/2/4 short rows), so there is no overflow to scroll and the 'can't reach Clear All Data' scenario does not manifest. Real but cosmetic -> P3, not a P1 scroll-broken defect.

title: Backup 'Import' requires typing/pasting JSON into an editable GuidedAction inline editor — a 10-foot IME flow that is hostile on phone
symptom: On a phone, restoring a backup means tapping the 'Import Backup' row, which opens Leanback's inline guided edit field, and pasting a long multi-line JSON blob into it, then tapping 'Restore from Backup'. There is no file picker, no clipboard affordance, and the inline editor plus soft keyboard fight for the small portrait screen. The .ooubackup file that Export produces can't be selected back — the user must manually obtain its JSON text and paste it. Most phone users cannot complete a restore.
rootCause: ACTION_IMPORT is built .descriptionEditable(true) with TYPE_CLASS_TEXT | TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_MULTI_LINE (BackupFragment.kt:44-45). The restore handler reads that editable description back as the JSON source (BackupFragment.kt:71) and passes it to viewModel.importBackup(json) (BackupViewModel.kt:39-44 -> backupService.importBackup(json)). VERIFIED: grep for ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT / registerForActivityResult / GetContent across the backup package returns nothing — there is no Storage Access Framework picker anywhere. The only restore input path is the pasted text.
fix: On phone (DeviceUtils.isPhone()), replace the editable-action paste flow with ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT (SAF) for the .ooubackup file, read the stream, and feed it to viewModel.importBackup(). For export, surface ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT or a share sheet. Keep the editable-GuidedAction paste path only for TV. This also removes the inline editor from expanding inside the actions list.

title: Update/Backup/Clear screens are a horizontal two-pane TV guidance layout with no phone/portrait arrangement
symptom: On a phone these render as the Leanback two-pane guidance composition: a guidance block (title/description/breadcrumb) on the LEFT and focus-styled action rows on the RIGHT, side-by-side, squeezed into portrait. It reads as a TV settings panel, not a Material screen, with oversized guidance text and big focus-tinted rows occupying only ~half the width.
rootCause: VERIFIED in leanback-1.0.0.aar res/layout/lb_guidedstep_fragment.xml: the root content_frame is a HORIZONTAL LinearLayout (line 35) with content_fragment (guidance, weight 1, line 40-44) and action_fragment_root (actions pane, line 46-56) side-by-side. Each fragment only supplies GuidanceStylist.Guidance + GuidedAction lists (UpdateFragment.kt:32-59, BackupFragment.kt:21-64, ClearConfirmFragment.kt:10-32) — the layout is framework-driven, so there is no layout/ vs layout-television/ variant to give phones a portrait composition. SettingsFragment.navigateToFragment (SettingsFragment.kt:353-358) routes to BackupFragment()/UpdateFragment() with no DeviceUtils.isPhone() branch (verified: grep for isPhone/isTV/DeviceUtils in SettingsFragment returns nothing).
fix: Branch on DeviceUtils.isPhone() in SettingsFragment.onGuidedActionClicked (lines 242/244): route ACTION_UPDATE/ACTION_BACKUP to phone-native fragments (Material toolbar + vertical scrolling list/buttons) on phone, GuidedStep only on TV. Make ClearConfirm an android.app.AlertDialog on phone (matching the app's other Leanback-safe confirm dialogs). Note SettingsFragment itself is also a GuidedStepSupportFragment (SettingsFragment.kt:35), so the whole settings entry is TV-shaped on phone — consolidate with the broader Settings/Parental/Subtitle GuidedStep phone-rewrite (already noted as deferred to a future release in CLAUDE.md v3.7.11).

title: Tapping an empty slot does nothing on phone — channel picker only opens on long-press; both entry points seed nothing
symptom: A phone user enters MultiView from the Home hero card or the Live TV header icon — BOTH call navigateToMultiView() with no seed channel — and lands on four empty 'Welcome to MultiView' slots. Tapping any empty slot does nothing visible (it only re-selects the slot and flashes controls). The empty-state overlay says 'Press OK to pick a channel', but a phone has no OK button. The only way to fill a slot is an undiscoverable long-press. The screen is effectively unusable on touch entry.
rootCause: In setupSlotViews() the phone branch (gated on !DeviceUtils.isTV, MultiViewFragment.kt:198) wires slotFrames[i].setOnClickListener (lines 199-205) to only setFocusedSlot / setAudioSlot / requestFocus / showControls() — it never calls openChannelPicker. The D-pad path opens the picker for an empty slot at onFullKeyEvent ACTION_UP line 682 (slot.channel == null -> openChannelPicker(focused)); touch has no equivalent. setOnLongClickListener (line 206) opens the picker, but only via long-press. Verified that MainActivity.navigateToMultiView (line 438) defaults seedChannel=null, and both real callers (HomeFragment.kt:694, LiveTvFragment.kt:218) pass nothing — so a touch user always starts with empty slots and cannot fill them by tapping.
fix: In the phone setOnClickListener at MultiViewFragment.kt:199, branch on slot occupancy: if viewModel.slots.value[i].channel == null, call openChannelPicker(i) (mirroring the D-pad empty-slot path at line 682); only when occupied should it fall through to setAudioSlot/showControls. Keep long-press as the change/swap/remove menu for occupied slots. Also fix the empty-state instruction (fragment_multiview.xml:154 'Press OK to pick a channel') to be touch-aware, e.g. 'Tap a screen to pick a channel' on phone.
correction: Severity raised P1 -> P0. The auditor under-rated this: because BOTH MultiView entry points (HomeFragment.kt:694 and LiveTvFragment.kt:218) call navigateToMultiView() with no seed, every touch user lands on four empty slots, and tap is the only intuitive gesture. With tap doing nothing and the on-screen hint telling them to 'Press OK' (a button phones lack), the feature is unusable on touch entry, not merely degraded. Long-press technically works but is undiscoverable, which does not save it from P0. Root cause and fix as written are accurate.

title: Layout-mode switcher (2x2/1+3/Dual/Triple) and the whole top/bottom control bar start GONE and auto-hide in 8s
symptom: A phone user has no obvious way to change the grid layout or pick the audio slot. The top bar (layout buttons) AND the bottom bar (audio slot buttons) are both hidden on entry; they only appear after tapping a slot, then disappear again after 8 seconds. Users may never realize the layouts exist.
rootCause: Both <include android:id="@+id/top_bar"> (fragment_multiview.xml:113) and <include android:id="@+id/bottom_bar"> (line 122) are android:visibility="gone" by default. They are only revealed by showControls() (line 580-586, sets both VISIBLE), whose only phone trigger is a slot tap (setOnClickListener line 204). resetControlsTimer() (line 593-599) then hides them after CONTROLS_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000ms (line 85). The layout buttons themselves have working click listeners (MultiViewTopBarController.setLayoutClickListener line 63-83), so the issue is purely discoverability/reachability of the bars, not click handling.
fix: On phone (DeviceUtils.isPhone), keep the top and bottom bars visible (skip the gone default and/or skip the auto-hide timer on phone entry), or add a persistent floating layout/menu FAB. At minimum, do not start the controls auto-hide timer on a phone so the bars stay up until a deliberate dismiss.
correction: Confirmed at P2; root cause verified. Note the auditor scoped this to the top bar only — the BOTTOM bar (audio-slot selector) is gone-by-default and auto-hides with the SAME root cause (showControls() at line 580 toggles both, resetControlsTimer hides both). The audio-slot buttons are therefore equally unreachable on touch. Folding it into this finding rather than a separate one since the mechanism is identical.

title: Top-bar layout buttons and bottom-bar audio buttons are well under the 48dp touch-target minimum
symptom: The 2x2/1+3/Dual/Triple buttons and the numbered audio buttons are small, tightly-packed text pills that are hard to hit accurately with a finger; mis-taps land on the adjacent button.
rootCause: Layout buttons are TextViews with textSize 10sp and paddingVertical 6dp only (view_multiview_top_bar.xml:72-75) — roughly 13-17dp text box + 12dp vertical padding = ~27-29dp total height, far below 48dp; horizontal padding is 14dp with no inter-button margin so they abut. Audio buttons are built in MultiViewBottomBarController.setupAudioButtons with textSize 11f and 6dp vertical padding (lines 51-58) = ~27dp, also under 48dp, with only a 4dp marginStart between them (line 71).
fix: On phone, set minWidth/minHeight to 48dp (programmatically minimumHeight = (48 * density) in MultiViewTopBarController/MultiViewBottomBarController, or via values-sw320dp dimens applied to these views) and increase inter-button spacing to >=8dp so finger targets don't overlap.

title: No on-screen back/close control — exit depends entirely on the system back gesture
symptom: On a phone there is no visible way to leave MultiView; the user must know to use the system back gesture/button. With the control bars hidden by default and no close icon, a touch user can feel trapped. (System back does work — it is routed correctly — so this is friction, not a dead end.)
rootCause: Grep of fragment_multiview.xml, view_multiview_top_bar.xml, and view_multiview_bottom_bar.xml confirms there is no back/close affordance — only a non-interactive '[Back] Exit' text hint (view_multiview_bottom_bar.xml:108). Exit is wired solely through onKeyEvent KEYCODE_BACK -> showExitDialog() (MultiViewFragment.kt:699-719), and showExitDialog() (line 1067) calls parentFragmentManager.popBackStack() (line 1072). System back reaches this via MainActivity.dispatchKeyEvent -> fragment.onKeyEvent (MainActivity.kt:292-294), so back is functional; there is just no touch button.
fix: Add a phone-only circular back/close button overlaid top-left of the grid (reuse the PhoneToolbarHelper pattern used on VodDetail/SeriesDetail) that calls showExitDialog() (or parentFragmentManager.popBackStack() directly).
correction: Confirmed at P2. The auditor's claim that the user is 'trapped' is overstated — the system back gesture/button IS correctly routed (MainActivity.kt:292 -> onKeyEvent KEYCODE_BACK -> showExitDialog -> popBackStack), so exit works. This is discoverability friction, not an unescapable screen. P2 (noticeable friction) is the right severity; it is not a P0/P1 dead end.

title: Bottom-bar EPG ticker is an auto-scroll marquee that cannot be finger-dragged
symptom: The 'NOW PLAYING' ticker scrolls itself back and forth; a phone user who tries to swipe it to read ahead cannot — the running animator immediately overrides the drag and the ticker keeps its own ping-pong pace.
rootCause: ticker_scroll is a HorizontalScrollView (view_multiview_bottom_bar.xml:34) whose scrollX is driven by an ObjectAnimator (startTickerScroll, MultiViewBottomBarController.kt:159-173) with repeatCount INFINITE and repeatMode REVERSE. A HorizontalScrollView is touch-draggable by default, but because the animator continuously writes scrollX every frame, any user drag is instantly overwritten. There is also no affordance suggesting it is interactive — it is a marquee, not a scroll surface.
fix: Acceptable as a marquee at this priority. If touch-read-ahead is desired, pause the animator on ACTION_DOWN and resume on ACTION_UP/idle so the user can drag-scroll. Otherwise leave as-is.

title: Bottom action-button row overflows / squashes below 48dp on phones with no horizontal scroll
symptom: On a ~360dp phone the VOD/Series controls bar packs 10 action buttons into a fixed full-width row with no horizontal scroll (Prev, -10s, Play, +10s, Next, Aspect, CC, Audio, External, Stats — Stats is phone-only so phone is the worst case with 10 vs TV's 9). With each button now carrying minimumWidth=48dp the row's measured content (~480dp) exceeds the screen; gravity=center then centers the overflow and clips the leftmost (Prev) and rightmost (Stats/External) buttons off both edges, making them untappable. Where weight wins instead, every button is squeezed icon+label below the 48dp Material tap target and is hard to hit precisely.
rootCause: action_buttons_row (overlay_player_controls.xml:230) is a plain horizontal LinearLayout, layout_width=match_parent, gravity=center, NOT wrapped in a HorizontalScrollView. Each button is added by addActionButton()/addCcButton() with LinearLayout.LayoutParams(0, WRAP_CONTENT, 1f) (PlayerControlsBar.kt:476, 404) so they share width by weight, AND v3.7.11 added minimumWidth = dp(48) (PlayerControlsBar.kt:485). 10 children × 48dp = 480dp + bottom_controls 32dp+32dp side margins exceeds a phone's usable width. LinearLayout's horizontal measure honors each child's minimumWidth, so the row overflows its (non-scrollable) parent and the centered overflow is clipped. There is no scroll affordance to reach overflowed buttons. Confirmed VOD/Series count = 10 (setupVodActionButtons, lines 383-398) and Live = 7 on phone (setupLiveActionButtons, 369-381). No clipChildren=false on the row or bottom_controls.
fix: Wrap action_buttons_row in a HorizontalScrollView (android:scrollbars=none, fillViewport=false) so the full set is reachable by horizontal drag on phone; switch addActionButton/addCcButton from weight (0dp,1f) to WRAP_CONTENT width with a fixed marginEnd and a real 48dp tap zone so they scroll instead of squash. Or, on phone (!DeviceUtils.isTV), collapse secondary actions (External, Stats, CC) into an overflow '…' button. Keep the weighted full-width layout for TV only (gravity=center reads well at 10ft).
correction: Confirmed real. Verified VOD/Series row is 10 buttons on phone (setupVodActionButtons 383-398 + phone-only Stats), TV is 9, and minimumWidth=dp(48) is applied per button (PlayerControlsBar.kt:485). The row is a plain LinearLayout not inside a HorizontalScrollView, with gravity=center and no clipChildren override. The auditor's overflow/clip-vs-squash analysis is accurate; the exact split between 'clipped off-edge' and 'squashed under 48dp' is device-width dependent but the user-observable harm (edge buttons unreachable / hard to hit) holds either way. Severity P1 confirmed: player still functions, but some controls are not reliably tappable.

title: Phone gesture suite (double-tap seek, drag volume/brightness, fling zap, long-press 2x, pinch) is dead while the controls bar is visible
symptom: After the user single-taps to reveal the controls bar (or it auto-shows on double-tap/seek), every phone gesture — double-tap-to-seek, vertical drag for brightness/volume, horizontal fling to zap channel / coarse-seek, long-press 2× speed, pinch aspect — stops working for the full 15s auto-hide window. A touch anywhere over the video only dismisses the bar. The gesture suite feels intermittent/broken.
rootCause: The PlayerControlsBar is added to the fragment root as a MATCH_PARENT/MATCH_PARENT FrameLayout (OoustreamPlaybackFragment.kt:748-755), added AFTER the SurfaceView/TextureView so it sits on top in z-order. Its root FrameLayout has setOnClickListener { onScrimTap?.invoke() } (PlayerControlsBar.kt:98), wired to controlsManager?.hide() (OoustreamPlaybackFragment.kt:776), which makes the entire overlay clickable and therefore touch-consuming. The fragment's gesture touchListener is attached only to rootView (line 2542) and to descendant SurfaceView/TextureView (attachToSurfaces, 2547-2555) — NOT to the controls bar overlay. So while the bar is VISIBLE it intercepts ACTION_DOWN over the whole screen before the gesture pipeline (gestureDetector/scaleDetector) ever sees it. Auto-hide is 15s (PlayerControlsManager.kt:21), so the dead window is long.
fix: Forward touches from the controls bar to the gesture pipeline when they fall outside the actual control widgets. Either (a) give the bar's full-screen scrim its own GestureDetector mirroring the fragment's (double-tap/drag/fling) and treat only a simple tap as hide; or (b) make the bar root non-clickable and attach the fragment's same touchListener to the controls bar root, letting onSingleTapConfirmed toggle visibility. Children (action button row, seek bar, play/pause) keep their own click handling because they're above the scrim. Reset the auto-hide timer on any forwarded gesture.
correction: Confirmed real. Verified: setupTouchGestures(view) is called with the same 'view' the controls bar is added to (line 923 + 749), the bar is MATCH_PARENT and z-ordered above the surfaces, the bar root has a click listener (PlayerControlsBar.kt:98) wired to hide (line 776), and the gesture touchListener is bound only to rootView + SurfaceView/TextureView (2542-2555), never to the controls bar. Auditor's mechanism is exactly right. Added detail: auto-hide is 15s (PlayerControlsManager.kt:21), so the gesture-dead window is a full 15 seconds per reveal — strengthens P1.

title: Pinch-to-zoom aspect gesture is non-reversible (zoom-out does the same thing as zoom-in)
symptom: Pinching out (zoom in) and pinching in (zoom out) both advance the aspect-ratio cycle in the same direction. A user cannot pinch the opposite way to step back. Contradicts the natural 'pinch in = less zoom' mental model. In practice the impact is tiny because there are only two modes (Fit / Crop-Fill), so a single pinch either way always lands on the other mode — you can never actually get 'stuck'.
rootCause: onScaleEnd calls cycleAspectRatio() for BOTH accumulatedScale > 1.15f and accumulatedScale < 0.85f (OoustreamPlaybackFragment.kt:2514-2515, explicit comment 'single direction list — same call'). cycleAspectRatio() only does currentScalingMode = (currentScalingMode + 1) % scalingModes.size (line 3076), and scalingModes has just 2 entries (line 3069-3072, labels 'Fit'/'Crop/Fill' at 3073) — no decrement path.
fix: On accumulatedScale < 0.85f step backward: currentScalingMode = (currentScalingMode - 1 + scalingModes.size) % scalingModes.size, instead of calling the forward cycle. One-line branch. With only 2 modes the visible difference is negligible, so this is pure polish.
correction: Confirmed real but practically moot. Verified scalingModes has exactly 2 entries (lines 3069-3073) and both pinch directions call the same forward cycleAspectRatio(). Because there are only two modes, one pinch in EITHER direction always reaches the other mode, so the 'can't go back' symptom never actually strands the user. P3 is correct (arguably even cosmetic). Auditor's code reading is accurate.

title: Login card has no scroll container and the Activity sets no windowSoftInputMode — soft keyboard can hide the Sign In button and error text
symptom: On a phone, the username field auto-focuses on load (LoginFragment.kt:84 usernameInput.post { requestFocus() }), so the soft keyboard pops up immediately on first run. The login card cannot scroll, and the window has no defined keyboard behavior, so on a short phone the IME can push/cover the lower form. The 'Sign In' Button (4th child) and the status/error TextView (5th child, where login errors render) sit below the password field and can be occluded by the keyboard with no scroll recovery — user can type credentials but can't reach Submit and never sees error text.
rootCause: fragment_login.xml root is a FrameLayout (match_parent) wrapping a single centered LinearLayout (480dp wide, height=wrap_content, layout_gravity=center) — VERIFIED: no ScrollView/NestedScrollView anywhere in the file. The host container main_container (activity_main.xml:10-14) is a bare FrameLayout that even carries layout_marginBottom=@dimen/bottom_nav_height (reserving space for the bottom nav), further compressing vertical room — and it has no scroll wrapper either. On phone, MainActivity.kt:65-67 applies Theme.Ooustream.Mobile (Theme.MaterialComponents.NoActionBar); neither that theme (themes_mobile.xml) nor the manifest .MainActivity entry (AndroidManifest.xml:34-39) sets android:windowSoftInputMode, and a project-wide grep for windowSoftInputMode/SOFT_INPUT returns NOTHING — so the IME runs with the default SOFT_INPUT_ADJUST_UNSPECIFIED. With non-scrollable content the system pan/resize behavior can clip the bottom controls with no scroll fallback. LoginFragment.kt:84 force-focuses the username field on load, triggering the IME on entry.
fix: Wrap the centered LinearLayout in a ScrollView/NestedScrollView with android:fillViewport="true" and android:layout_height="match_parent" (set the ScrollView's gravity=center so the card stays centered when there's room but can scroll when the IME is up). AND set android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize" — either on the .MainActivity entry in AndroidManifest.xml:34-39, or in Theme.Ooustream.Mobile (themes_mobile.xml) so only the phone path gets it. Additionally guard the auto-focus at LoginFragment.kt:84 to only requestFocus() on TV (if (DeviceUtils.isTV(requireContext()))) so phones don't auto-pop the keyboard on first launch.
correction: Confirmed as-is. All claims verified against code: no scroll container in fragment_login.xml, no windowSoftInputMode anywhere in src, auto-focus at line 84 fires the IME on load. One added detail the auditor missed: the host main_container (activity_main.xml:14) also reserves bottom_nav_height as a bottom margin, eating additional vertical space and making the occlusion worse on short phones — reinforces P0.

title: Login card hardcoded to 480dp width — wider than most phones in portrait, content clipped with no horizontal scroll
symptom: On a typical 360dp-wide phone (and worse on 320dp small phones), the centered login card (fixed 480dp) is wider than the screen. Because the root FrameLayout centers it (layout_gravity=center), the card's left/right edges and its rounded bg_login_card background are clipped equally on both sides, and the 40dp internal padding eats further into usable width. There is no horizontal scroll, so the card just gets cut off and looks broken / not phone-designed.
rootCause: fragment_login.xml line 10: the card LinearLayout uses a hardcoded android:layout_width="480dp" with android:padding="40dp" (line 15). 480dp exceeds common phone widths (360dp) and small phones (320dp). VERIFIED there is no phone/portrait layout variant — only layout/ and layout-television/ exist (fragment_login.xml exists ONLY in layout/, shared by phone and TV), and no dimen indirection for this width, so the TV-sized card renders verbatim on phones. The child EditTexts are layout_width=match_parent so they stay within the (clipped) card, which is why the inputs remain partially usable — degraded, not unusable.
fix: Make the card width responsive: change line 10 to android:layout_width="match_parent" with horizontal margins (e.g. android:layout_marginStart/End="24dp"), or wrap in a ConstraintLayout with android:maxWidth="480dp". Extract 480dp to @dimen/login_card_width and override in values-television/ (keep 480dp for TV) vs values/ (match_parent/responsive for phone). Reduce padding from 40dp to a smaller @dimen on phones.
correction: Confirmed as-is. Verified line 10 is android:layout_width="480dp" and confirmed no portrait/phone layout variant exists (only layout/ and layout-television/). P1 severity is correct — clipping is centered so inputs stay reachable, screen is degraded but usable.

title: Login button rendered permanently at alpha 0.9 (and dims further) on phones with no focus concept
symptom: On a phone the 'Sign In' button always appears slightly faded (90% opacity) because the alpha=0.9 dim is a TV focus affordance that never gets restored to 1.0 — the restore only happens on a D-pad focus event, which never fires on touch. During loading it correctly drops to 0.5 alpha, but in idle/error states it stays at 0.9, looking subtly disabled rather than tappable. There is also no ripple/touch feedback on tap.
rootCause: LoginFragment.kt line 81 sets loginButton.alpha = 0.9f as an unfocused-state dim; the focus listener (lines 57-78) only restores alpha=1.0f inside the hasFocus branch (line 67), which never triggers on touch. The auth-state observer resets to 0.9f on Idle (line 114) and Error (line 109). VERIFIED there is no android:foreground/selectableItemBackground ripple on the button in fragment_login.xml. This is a 10-foot focus cue applied unconditionally to phones.
fix: Gate the alpha dim + focus-scale animation behind DeviceUtils.isTV(requireContext()): on phone, set loginButton.alpha = 1.0f always and skip setOnFocusChangeListener; in the auth-state observer use 1.0f (not 0.9f) for Idle/Error on phone. Add android:foreground="?android:attr/selectableItemBackground" (or a ripple) to the Button in fragment_login.xml for touch feedback.
correction: Confirmed as-is. Verified lines 81, 99, 109, 114 set alpha and the focus listener only restores full alpha on D-pad focus. Confirmed no ripple foreground on the button. P3 polish severity is correct.

title: Intro splash can only be skipped by a key/D-pad event, not by tapping the screen
symptom: On a phone, a user who wants to skip the intro video taps the screen and nothing happens — they must wait for the video to end (STATE_ENDED) or the 5s timeout. There is no touch affordance to skip.
rootCause: IntroSplashFragment dismisses only via onKeyEvent (lines 97-103, fired by MainActivity key dispatch / D-pad), STATE_ENDED (line 56), onPlayerError (line 59), or the 5000ms timeout (lines 68-71). The PlayerView is created with useController=false (line 38) and no setOnClickListener / GestureDetector is attached. VERIFIED MainActivity has no dispatchTouchEvent/onTouchEvent path to forward a tap to the splash. So touch events do nothing.
fix: In onViewCreated, on phone (if (!DeviceUtils.isTV(requireContext()))) add playerView?.setOnClickListener { skip() } (or a GestureDetector single-tap) so a tap skips the intro, mirroring the key-to-skip behavior. Low urgency since the 5s cap bounds the wait.
correction: Confirmed as-is. Verified useController=false (line 38), skip paths are key/timeout/end-only, and no touch listener is attached. Also confirmed MainActivity has no dispatchTouchEvent/onTouchEvent forwarding, so a tap truly cannot reach skip(). P3 is correct (5s cap bounds the wait).

title: [MISSED] Password field declares imeOptions=actionDone but no editor-action listener — pressing keyboard Done does nothing, so the only IME fallback to submit when the button is occluded also fails
symptom: On a phone, after typing the password the user presses the keyboard's Done/checkmark key (the natural way to submit when the on-screen button is hidden under the IME) — and nothing happens. The form does not log in. Combined with the P0 button-occlusion, this leaves the user with NO way to submit: the Sign In button is under the keyboard and the keyboard's own Done action is dead.
rootCause: passwordInput declares android:imeOptions="actionDone" (fragment_login.xml line 73), which paints a Done action on the IME — but LoginFragment never calls passwordInput.setOnEditorActionListener(...) (VERIFIED: grep for setOnEditorActionListener/OnEditorAction/IME_ACTION returns nothing). The only path that calls viewModel.login(...) is loginButton.setOnClickListener (LoginFragment.kt:49-54). So the Done key is wired to nothing.
fix: In onViewCreated add passwordInput.setOnEditorActionListener { _, actionId, _ -> if (actionId == EditorInfo.IME_ACTION_DONE) { loginButton.performClick(); true } else false }. This gives a working IME-driven submit that survives the keyboard-occlusion case (and is the standard mobile login pattern). Should ship together with the P0 scroll/adjustResize fix.
correction: [MISSED] The auditor flagged the button occlusion (P0) but did not notice that the keyboard's own Done action — the natural fallback submit when the button is hidden — is unwired. Verified: imeOptions=actionDone is set in XML but no setOnEditorActionListener exists in LoginFragment. This turns the P0 occlusion into a hard dead-end on short phones, so it's a real P1 touch-usability defect.

title: Permanent 56dp bottom margin on main_container leaves a dead black bar under fullscreen player / MultiView / Login on phone
symptom: On a phone, opening fullscreen video, MultiView, the splash, or Login leaves a ~56dp black strip pinned to the bottom of the screen. The bottom nav is correctly hidden (View.GONE via syncBottomNav), but the hosted fragment content does not expand to fill that reserved space — it stays inset, so 'fullscreen' video/MultiView is visibly short at the bottom.
rootCause: layout/activity_main.xml line 14: main_container has a static android:layout_marginBottom="@dimen/bottom_nav_height". On phone @dimen/bottom_nav_height = 56dp (values/dimens.xml line 69); on TV it is 0dp (values-television/dimens.xml line 46, and the TV layout-television/activity_main.xml omits the attribute entirely). main_container and the BottomNavigationView are siblings in a FrameLayout, so setting the nav GONE (MainActivity.syncBottomNav line 172) does NOT collapse main_container's fixed margin. Verified there is NO code anywhere that zeroes/restores bottomMargin (grep for main_container+margin/layoutParams and bottomMargin/setMargins in MainActivity both empty). The player and MultiView are committed into R.id.main_container via .replace(), with no separate full-window surface (no addContentView; only window FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON / brightness flags touched), so the margin truly insets their content.
fix: Toggle the margin alongside visibility, or restructure to a weighted layout. Lowest-risk: in syncBottomNav(), when hideNav==true set ((ViewGroup.MarginLayoutParams) mainContainer.layoutParams).bottomMargin = 0 and requestLayout(); when false restore resources.getDimensionPixelSize(R.dimen.bottom_nav_height). Cleaner long-term: wrap main_container + bottom_navigation in a vertical LinearLayout (container height=0dp, weight=1) and drop the marginBottom; that also resolves the splash/login overlap in nav-bottomnav-over-login-splash.

title: Bottom nav is shown over the splash and the first-launch Login screen; tabs are tappable while unauthenticated
symptom: On first launch (not yet logged in) a phone user sees the bottom nav (Home/Live/Movies/Series/Search) overlaid on the splash and then on Login. The tabs are tappable before login — tapping one (navigateFromSidebar) replaces the LoginFragment with a content fragment that has no credentials, dropping the user into an empty/broken screen instead of letting them log in. Same on logout-to-login.
rootCause: BottomNavigationView in activity_main.xml (lines 23-32) has NO android:visibility, so it defaults VISIBLE. The only code that hides it is syncBottomNav() (MainActivity lines 157-172), which is invoked ONLY from the back-stack-changed listener (line 153) and from navigateToHome() (line 435). The splash is committed with .commit() (lines 90-92) and the first-launch LoginFragment with .commitAllowingStateLoss() (lines 85-88) — neither uses addToBackStack, so neither fires a back-stack change and syncBottomNav() never runs; the nav stays VISIBLE. syncBottomNav() already classifies IntroSplashFragment and LoginFragment as hideNav==true (line 171), so it WOULD hide the bar if it were called. The auto-login path is fine (it routes through navigateToHome → syncBottomNav). Also confirmed: navigateToLogin() (lines 446-453) does NOT call syncBottomNav() either, so logout also strands the bar over Login.
fix: Set android:visibility="gone" on the BottomNavigationView in XML so it is hidden until an authenticated top-level fragment is shown, AND/OR explicitly call syncBottomNav() after the splash commit (line 92), after the first-launch LoginFragment commit (line 88), and in navigateToLogin() (after line 452). Because syncBottomNav already treats both fragments as hideNav==true, invoking it on those paths fixes the overlap with no further logic.

title: Favorites and Settings are unreachable by touch from Live TV / VOD / Series / Search
symptom: A phone user browsing Live TV, Movies, Series, or Search has no on-screen control to open Favorites or Settings. They must tap the Home tab (or press Back) to return to Home, then tap the Favorites section card or the gear icon in the Home header. Settings/Favorites are effectively two steps deep and hidden from most of the app.
rootCause: bottom_nav_menu.xml defines only 5 destinations (nav_home, nav_live, nav_movies, nav_series, nav_search) — no Favorites, no Settings. Those two are surfaced ONLY on Home: Settings via the header_settings icon (HomeFragment.setupHeaderIcons line 623-624 → navigateToSection("settings")) and Favorites via a section card dispatched in navigateToSection (HomeFragment line 1899). grep of livetv/, vod/, series/, search/ packages for SettingsFragment/FavoritesFragment returns nothing — no entry point there. On TV these are reached via QuickSidebar, but the sidebar is gated TV-only (MainActivity.isSidebarAllowedForCurrentFragment line 196 returns false on phone), leaving phone with no global access.
fix: Give phone a persistent route to Settings and Favorites from any screen. Lowest-risk: add a shared top header (reuse include_screen_header) carrying the existing Settings gear + a Favorites star to LiveTvFragment / VodFragment / SeriesFragment / SearchFragment, OR add an overflow/'More' action. Keep the bottom nav at 5 items rather than cramming 6+ tabs on small phones.
correction: Confirmed reachability gap, but recategorize the user impact: this is a nav-reachability/UX-depth issue, NOT the user's 'menus not scrolling' complaint. P2 is correct (friction, not unusable — the destinations ARE reachable via Home in 2 taps). Not a scroll/touch-target defect.
